findings.title: Schedules that ended months ago are still measured in 109 counties, not only NCTD's; section 9 does not say so
findings.quote: NCTD's current copy also answers 403, so San Diego measures NCTD on its legacy-mirror schedule (29 Jul 2026);
findings.problem: Section 9 presents San Diego's July NCTD schedule as a download problem. Its only other lapse rule is Dutchess's: a lapse within three weeks, measured while two full Wednesdays remain. It does not say what happens to a copy whose whole bus schedule ended less than a year ago. Such a copy is measured on its last Wednesday with morning departures, and once it is read the step tries no other copy and no operator URL. This affects large systems, and a reader would take Atlanta's, San Francisco's or St. Louis's bus frequency as current. NEXT_ROUND item 8 treats NCTD as a download problem ('Retry each round'). But the pipeline never tries NCTD's own URL while the legacy mirror is under a year old, and no NEXT_ROUND item covers the other 43 feeds.
findings.evidence:
I compared feeds[].weekday with 'downloaded' in all 637 pipeline/data_*/transit_stops_7_9.meta.json. 130 county feeds (44 feeds, 109 counties) are measured on a Wednesday more than 21 days before the build, from a copy whose calendar ended before the build. They are 3 weeks to 11 months old. Examples:
- MARTA (368): 2026-08-19 in 12 counties. In Fulton 13121 it is the hosted copy, calendar 2026-04-18 to 2026-08-21, 6,886 stops; a HEAD of mdb-368/latest.zip shows last-modified 19 Apr 2026.
- SFMTA (2886): 2026-08-26 in 5 counties (06075: calendar to 2026-08-28).
- Milwaukee County Transit (2127): 2026-08-19 in 4 counties (55079 reads the legacy mirror).
- Metro St. Louis (190): 2026-06-10 in 6 counties.
- PSTA (326): 2026-06-03 in 3 counties.
- Also Sun Metro 2026-06-10, SunTran 2026-05-13 and Lane Transit 2026-01-28.
- Gold Coast (32): 2026-08-05 in 06083 and 06111. Its legacy mirror's bus dates run to 8 Aug 2026; NEXT_ROUND item 7 says 'to 5 Aug'.
The cause is in pipeline/fetch_oc.py lines 800–811: the next source is tried only after 'schedule ended over a year ago' or no bus service near today; otherwise the loop breaks.
For NCTD, cache/mdb/feeds_v2.csv lists mdb-3093 as active, with producer URL lfportal.nctd.org/staticGTFS/google_transit.zip. A HEAD of mdb-3093/latest.zip answers 403. data_06073's meta records only the legacy mirror (2025-10-12 to 2026-08-02, weekday 2026-07-29).
The round-8.4 audit already said this (logs/audit85_result.json, confirmed[49], corrected[0]): 'the pipeline does not try NCTD's own URL while its legacy-mirror schedule is under a year old'.
findings.fix: - **Schedules that have ended:** a feed copy whose bus schedule ended less than a year ago is measured on its last Wednesday with morning departures. No other copy or operator URL is then tried. 109 counties measure 44 such feeds, up to 11 months old: MARTA on 19 Aug 2026 (12 Atlanta-area counties), SFMTA on 26 Aug, Milwaukee County Transit on 19 Aug, Metro St. Louis on 10 Jun, PSTA on 3 Jun, and Gold Coast on 5 Aug. NCTD is one of them: MobilityData's hosted copy answers 403, so the legacy mirror (to 2 Aug 2026) is read, and NCTD's own URL is not tried. San Diego measures NCTD on 29 Jul 2026. (Add a NEXT_ROUND item: when a copy's schedule has ended, try the next copy and the operator's URL.)
